title: Revealing the Spin Hydrodynamics of a Spin-Imbalanced Unitary Fermi Gas
authors: DeChao Zhang, Johannes Lang, J. E. Thomas
abstract: Hydrodynamics governs diverse collective phenomena in nature, from the expansion of a quarkgluon plasma to viscous electron flow in quantum materials. In strongly interacting hydrodynamic fluids, the transport of spin remains poorly understood. Here, we investigate spin transport in the hydrodynamic regime of a spin-imbalanced unitary Fermi gas confined in a uniform optical box. By quenching a spatially periodic optical potential that modulates both the density and spin polarization, we observe the relaxation of the many-body system, which determines both the spin diffusivity and the spin Seebeck/Peltier coefficients in a homogeneous quantum gas. Our measurements provide parameter-free benchmarks for microscopic theories and establish an ultracold atom platform for studying spin caloritronics in strongly correlated matter.
summary: The authors investigate spin hydrodynamics in a spin-imbalanced unitary Fermi gas using an ultracold atom setup. By analyzing the relaxation dynamics following periodic perturbations, they extract fundamental transport coefficients like spin diffusivity and the energy-spin Seebeck coefficient. This work establishes a quantitative experimental platform for studying spin caloritronics in strongly correlated quantum matter.
main_problem: The study investigates spin transport, specifically spin hydrodynamics and spin caloritronics, which remains poorly understood in strongly interacting quantum fluids.
main_result: The experiment successfully measures fundamental energy and spin current coefficients ($	ilde{D}_s$ and $	ilde{S}_{\sigma}$), establishing a quantitative framework for universal spin hydrodynamics in the unitary Fermi gas.
method: Measurements involve quenching spatially periodic optical potentials to induce density and spin polarization modulations, followed by fitting the time evolution of these components using linear-response hydrodynamic models.
model_or_system: The system is a spin-imbalanced unitary Fermi gas (UFG) confined in an optical box. The dynamics are modeled using coupled differential equations describing perturbations in density, spin polarization, and temperature.
key_observables: Spin diffusivity ($	ilde{D}_s$), energy-spin Seebeck coefficient ($	ilde{S}_{\sigma}$), first sound diffusivity ($	ilde{D}_1$), and the evolution of polarization modulation $\delta P(q, t)$.
important_parameters: Polarization ($P$), reduced temperature ($T/T_F$), wavevector ($q$), and characteristic transport coefficients.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on linear-response theory, fitting data to hydrodynamic equations derived from irreversible thermodynamics, and utilizing the long wavelength limit for certain derivations.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the optical setup with periodic perturbations; subsequent figures show time evolution of Fourier components ($\delta P(q, t)$) and plots comparing extracted transport coefficients ($	ilde{S}_{\sigma}, 	ilde{D}_s, 	ilde{D}_1$) against theoretical predictions as a function of temperature or polarization.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the problem by detailing the experimental setup and measurement techniques. It then develops the hydrodynamic model governing spin and energy transport. Key results are presented through fitting data to extract universal dimensionless coefficients, culminating in consistency checks across different measurable quantities like $	ilde{D}_1$.
why_interesting: This work provides direct, quantitative measurements of spin-dependent transport phenomena (spin Seebeck effect) in a highly controllable ultracold atomic platform, offering crucial benchmarks for theoretical models of strongly correlated quantum matter.
